correctness.rationale: For continuous positive data the unsymmetrized ratio expectation is one half of E[min/max], and the stated U-statistic has this expectation. Writing s2=EX² makes the fitted numerator mA+(s2−2m²)B−m²/2; direct integration for Beta(a,1) gives a(a−1)/[2(a+1)(2a+1)]. Scale invariance gives the entire uniform scale family. Near (1,1) the Beta integrals extend analytically using bounded kernels and integrable dominating powers of each endpoint. Differentiation along the two log-density scores yields 1/12 and (19−2π²)/12; the analytic implicit-function theorem gives a unique local branch a(b) with slope 2π²−19, with non-Gamma support. Independently differentiating the numerator at zero and adding both pairwise projections gives the stated fitted influence function. At uniform it is 3x−3x²+2x log x with variance 3/10−7/12+8/27=7/540. At the matching Gamma, scale invariance permits Gamma(3,1); exact factorial integrals of the squared exponential polynomials give 37/2592. The requisite fourth moments for the sample-second-moment CLT exist under both laws (finite second moment alone would not justify a general CLT). For central two-sided Gamma calibration that refits by moments, null-variance continuity at shape 3 follows from continuous conditional kernel means and uniform moment bounds on a compact shape interval; the stated consistent calibration has asymptotic scaled cutoffs ±z√(37/2592). The alternative variance therefore gives 2Φ(−z√(185/168))≈0.0397113 at 5%. The original uncensored preprint allows generic consistent estimates; moment fitting is the explicitly selected variant here, and this power does not follow from its printed plug-in asymptotics or an unrefitted implementation. Its fixed-parameter projection at Gamma(3,1) differs and has variance 521/324. The frozen checker was inspected, not run.

value.rationale: A published scalar goodness-of-fit procedure can miss a familiar bounded-support alternative even though its fitted Gamma matches both moments. The analytic neighborhood shows robust nonidentification on an explicit two-shape slice rather than a single coincidence. Accounting for refitting changes the null asymptotics and gives a reproducible subnominal rejection limit with direct consequences for calibration. This is not a criticism of the separate squared-residual omnibus test and does not claim censoring or finite-sample conclusions.
